value.first: For the 3am wakings I'd use graduated check-ins, the Ferber method. It's one of the best-studied sleep methods there is, and the skill it teaches (falling asleep alone) is the same one he needs to fall back asleep at 3am. Start on a night that opens a clear week, no travel or illness. Bedtime is the same every night, between 6:30 and 8:00, with a 20-30 minute wind-down: bath, feed, book, bed. Put him in the crib drowsy but awake, say your goodnight phrase and leave.
value.second: When he cries, wait, then do a 1-2 minute check: lights off, calm voice, a short phrase, maybe a pat, no pickup, no feed. Night 1 waits are 3, 5, then 10 minutes, and 10 after that. Night 2: 5/10/12. Night 3: 10/12/15. Treat a 3am waking exactly like bedtime and restart that night's waits from the first one. Expect 30-60+ minutes of protest, and night 2 or 3 can be worse than night 1. That's the old pattern breaking, not failure. If you can't stand the waiting, the chair method is the gentler, slower version.
value.third: Nights 4-7 keep stretching: 12/15/17, then 15/17/20, then 17/20/25, then 20/25/30. By then many kids fall asleep in minutes, and 3am wakings usually settle soon after. Don't cave mid-wait, since that teaches longer crying. Call the doctor if you hear snoring or gasping in his sleep, or if he's still not improving after 7 consistent nights. I'll check in Thursday to hear how nights 1-3 went. Dr. Kurt Bjorkman, a pediatrician, has a good video on the evidence if you want it.
